They are not tied to credential theft, hidden loaders, attacker C2, or automatic exfiltration.
  • urllib.request.urlopen() in dcss_import.py appears to fetch Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup map data for an explicit map-generation tool; there is no evidence of install-time execution or sensitive-data upload.

Automatic Execution Paths

No confirmed malicious automatic execution path.

  • In the provided files, there is no evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, malicious install-time setup.py logic, abused PEP 517 build hooks, or import-time credential collection/exfiltration.
  • python/src/mettagrid/mapgen/tools/dcss_import.py contains if __name__ == "__main__": generate_scenes_from_dcss_maps(), which only runs when the script is invoked directly by a user.
  • subprocess.run findings in bazel_build.py appear consistent with a build helper script; the provided evidence does not show malicious execution during installation or interpreter startup.
  • Normal console_scripts or user-invoked CLI behavior is excluded because it is not evidence of malicious automatic execution.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

No confirmed evidence.

  • **Credential harvesting:** No evidence was provided of broad discovery of environment variables, .env, SSH keys, cloud credentials, npm/PyPI/GitHub tokens, CI/CD secrets, wallet files, or similar sensitive material.
  • **Exfiltration/staging:** No flow was identified that archives sensitive files with tar/zip/base64 and uploads them externally. .zip and wheel URLs in MODULE.bazel.lock appear to be dependency sources in a lockfile, not exfiltration evidence.
  • **Persistence:** No evidence of cron, systemd, launch agents, shell profile edits, startup folders, background polling, or self-reinstall logic.
  • **Lateral movement:** No evidence of Kubernetes service account use, Docker socket access, cloud metadata access, GitHub Actions token theft/workflow injection, or package registry token reuse.
  • **Obfuscation/loader:** The provided code does not show malicious eval/exec/compile, marshal/pickle staged loaders, encrypted payload decryption, or self-deleting droppers. The .json.z/.gz replay files appear to be compressed test data, though their contents were not fully validated.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • The many external URLs in MODULE.bazel.lock appear to be Bazel dependency lock metadata, with no confirmed attacker-controlled repository or typosquatting evidence.
